solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

definitions.note: adjective in both clue and answer

indicators.note: the words turn into something else, so their letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone who cheats ends up being obscure and hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' signals rearranging the twelve letters of A CHEAT SIMPLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphysical reasoning is notoriously abstract and difficult, hence a synonym for hard to understand.

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun 'one who puts things up'

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: An English parson does some building work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who erects or raises structures is literally the one who puts things up.

clue.text: Drinks for a trainee policeman on operations

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
a cop is a policeman
ops is short for operations

explanation.surface: Buying a round for a young police recruit out on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcopops are sweet, fruit-flavoured alcoholic drinks sold in bottles.

clue.text: Weed round first of seedlings and water

indicators.note: the tool word goes around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to hoe is to weed with a garden tool

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: weed around the young seedlings and water them.
explanation.definitionFit: To hose a garden is to spray it with water from a flexible pipe.

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A rowdy party down under gets out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' signals rearranging AUSTRALIAN; 'Wild' looks like a description of the party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman midwinter festival was famous for revelry, so the word now means any unrestrained party.

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
bunk means nonsense, rot

explanation.surface: A company acquires some beds for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a French landscape artist of the nineteenth century.

indicators.note: the article is seized and held inside the king's name

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: A monarch snatches a piece of writing out of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb but is the noun, animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal hide tanned for use is leather, so the noun senses match.

clue.text: What the chef could receive in perfect condition

definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: an order placed for a dessert of fruit in pastry
the idiom for everything neat and in its proper place

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes things arranged neatly, in a perfect state; literally, a request for a fruit dessert.

parts.note: a con is a convict, and the 's adds an S
descending means going down

explanation.surface: A stuck-up inmate is on the way down.
explanation.definitionFit: Being condescending means acting superior and patronising, which is what a snooty person does.

indicators.note: the abbreviation passes through the middle of the other word

parts.note: articles are items, pieces
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Something punches its way through a number of items.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and also builds the answer: R inside PIECES.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce things is to run a point through them, so the clue describes the action.

clue.text: Rent a fleece from a twister

parts.note: rent means torn, ripped
to do someone is to swindle or fleece them

explanation.surface: Tearing a wool garment off someone in a whirlwind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, popularly called a twister.

indicators.note: brought back, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to put an idea is to suggest it
IL is the Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: Proposing that the man from Italy came home drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lit up is slang for being tipsy or intoxicated.

parts.note: retched means vomited, was sick

explanation.surface: Apologising because a wife has thrown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' is the adjective meaning pitiful, not an apology.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorry state is a miserable or pitiable one, as is a wretched one.

clue.text: Who keeps steward excited in novel?

indicators.note: the outer word holds the rest inside it
stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking who restrains a frantic flight attendant in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' gives ESTWARD; 'keeps' holds it in WHO. 'novel' reads as an adjective meaning new, but it is the definition: a Victorian adventure book.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Kingsley's adventure book of 1855 bears this exclamatory title.

clue.text: Fairy meets goddess in place that's unimportant

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian myth

indicators.note: the goddess sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods

explanation.surface: A sprite encounters a deity somewhere of little significance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the edge rather than central is marginal and of minor significance.

parts.note: reads as a teacher governing a schoolchild's development, but means the part of the eye that sets the size of its opening, with 'She' as it is also a woman's name

explanation.definitionFit: The coloured ring of the eye widens or narrows the dark opening in its centre.

clue.text: Act I play out is unusual

indicators.note: the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: The first act of a play is out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, uncharacteristic, out of the ordinary.

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a lease is a rental agreement

explanation.surface: A rented property not yet up and running as an amenity.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility can mean skill without effort, a natural ease in doing something.

clue.text: Son joked and lost purchase on the road

parts.note: kidded means teased or joked

explanation.surface: A boy fooled around and then lost grip while driving.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that slides out of control has lost its grip, its traction, on the road.

clue.text: Band has drinks with ecstasy for entertainment

parts.note: a strip is a band of material
teas are drinks
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A music group enjoys drinks and drugs as part of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrobing to music is a form of entertainment found in clubs.

clue.text: Illness of worker eating rotten lime

indicators.note: the insect takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a worker is an ant in crosswords

indicators.note: gone bad, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A labourer falls ill after eating a bad citrus fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' gives ILME; 'eating' puts it in the insect. In crosswords 'worker' very often signals an ant or a bee.
explanation.definitionFit: An ailment is a minor illness or disorder.

clue.text: Scoundrel acquires popular firm making clothing

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Scoundrel acquires popular firm making clothing', lacks the 'a' of the published version ('Scoundrel acquires a popular firm...'): RAT around IN, CO and A needs that A.
annotationWithheld.clue: Scoundrel acquires popular firm making clothing

parts.note: owls are birds that hoot

explanation.surface: Something to cover a university's noisy birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowls are monks' hoods, garments covering the head.

clue.text: Pennies I spent put in a heap

parts.note: P stands for pence, pennies
to lead a life is to spend it, so spent gives led

explanation.surface: My coins, once paid out, were stacked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacked into a mound is exactly what piled means.

definitions.meaning: hard-shelled kernels such as walnuts or hazels
bats is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.definitionFit: Hard-shelled fruits, and also slang meaning crazy, like batty.

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective
an unsettled debt is owed

explanation.surface: Having one's goal outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Left in a will means bequeathed, which is to endow someone with property.

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
AN is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A family member owns a grubby piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean means not clean, soiled or dirty.

clue.text: Record playing well into the night? Very sad!

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
on means playing, as a show is on
so late means at a very late hour

explanation.surface: Neighbours playing music until the small hours is depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconsolate means unable to be comforted, deeply unhappy.
